issues.t: Heater core leaks coolant into the cabin
issues.sym: A sweet antifreeze smell from the vents, a greasy fog on the inside of the windshield that the defroster can't clear, wet carpet on the passenger side, or a coolant level that keeps dropping.
issues.why: The heater core or its gasket and O-rings leak inside the dash. Mitsubishi issued service bulletins on heater core and gasket leaks, and it is the most-reported Diamante complaint. Coolant can also drip onto the engine computer, causing warning lights or odd shifting.
issues.next: Don't drive if the windshield fogs so you can't see. Keep the coolant topped up and watch the temperature gauge. Have a shop confirm the leak and ask whether new gaskets alone will fix it before replacing the whole core.

issues.t: Automatic transmission fails early
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between gears, harsh shifts, or the car getting stuck in one gear (often third) with a warning light.
issues.why: RepairPal has dozens of reports of the Diamante's automatic transmission failing, at an average of about 115,000 miles. Mitsubishi also published transmission maintenance advice, since worn fluid makes problems worse.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition, and use only the fluid Mitsubishi specifies. If it is stuck in one gear, drive gently to a shop and have codes read before agreeing to a rebuild.

issues.t: Shudder or surge at 35–50 mph
issues.sym: A shudder, surge or vibration at steady speeds between about 35 and 50 mph, like driving over rumble strips.
issues.why: Mitsubishi bulletins say worn-out transmission fluid can make the torque converter lock-up clutch shudder.
issues.next: Ask a shop about Mitsubishi's torque converter shudder bulletin. A fluid change with the correct fluid often helps if done before the converter is damaged.

issues.t: Harsh or flaring 2-3 upshift
issues.sym: A hard bang or a quick rev flare when the transmission shifts from second to third.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued service bulletins for harsh 2-3 shifts on early cars and a 2-3 shift flare on 2003 and 2004 models.
issues.next: Have the fluid checked and ask about the shift bulletins. Adjustments or updates done early may avoid a rebuild.

issues.t: Car rocks or wanders from worn rear bushings
issues.sym: The car rocks side to side or feels loose over bumps and potholes, wanders in rain or snow, or the rear tires wear unevenly.
issues.why: The rear suspension knuckle bushings wear out with age; Mitsubishi issued a service manual update for replacing them. Worn struts add to the problem.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension bushings and struts inspected, then get an alignment after repairs.

issues.t: Vibration that increases with speed
issues.sym: A vibration through the car that gets stronger as speed rises.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued 2003 bulletins on vibration from the drive axles that increases with speed. Out-of-balance tires can feel similar.
issues.next: Have the tires balanced and checked first, then the drive axles and joints.

issues.t: Check engine light for a lean condition (P0171/P0174)
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P0171 and/or P0174, sometimes with a rough idle or hesitation.
issues.why: These codes mean the engine is getting too much air for the fuel being delivered. Mitsubishi issued 2002 bulletins on these codes for V6 models; vacuum leaks, a dirty airflow sensor or weak fuel delivery are common causes.
issues.next: Have a shop check for vacuum leaks and test the airflow sensor and fuel pressure before replacing parts.

issues.t: Steering wheel shudder or vibration
issues.sym: The steering wheel shakes or shudders while driving or turning.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued a 1998 bulletin for steering wheel shudder on these cars.
issues.next: Have the tires, wheels and steering parts checked and balanced.

issues.t: Squeal or chirp from the A/C belt idler pulley
issues.sym: A squeal, chirp or grinding from the front of the engine that may change when the A/C is on.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued bulletins on noise from the A/C belt idler pulley and later deleted that pulley on some cars.
issues.next: Have the belt and pulleys checked. A failed pulley can throw the belt and stop the A/C and other accessories.

issues.t: Parking brake clip screw can break (recall)
issues.sym: A parking brake that drags or won't hold, or a rear wheel that grabs or locks, especially on wet or snowy roads.
issues.why: The screw holding a rear parking brake shoe clip can become brittle and break, letting the clip come loose. Recall 00V132000 has dealers replace the screw and fix any damage.
issues.next: Ask a Mitsubishi dealer to check your VIN for recall 00V132000. If a rear wheel drags or grabs, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Engine can stall from wiring touching the heat shield (recall)
issues.sym: The engine runs erratically or shuts off suddenly while driving.
issues.why: On some 2002 cars, the engine wiring harness can rub on an exhaust heat shield and melt, shorting the crank angle sensor wiring. Recall 02V100001 has dealers inspect, repair and tie back the harness.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Ask a Mitsubishi dealer to check your VIN for recall 02V100001.

issues.t: Child seat tether instructions missing from manual (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The owner's manual lacks steps for adjusting the head restraint when using a child seat tether strap.
issues.why: If the tether strap is routed wrong, a child seat may not be held well in a crash. Recall 04V067000 sends owners a corrected instruction label for the manual.
issues.next: Follow the child seat maker's instructions carefully and ask a Mitsubishi dealer for the recall label.

issues.t: Fuel pump fails
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or it sputters and stalls, especially when the tank is low.
issues.why: Owners report fuel pump failures at around 60,000 miles on the 2000 Diamante.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested before replacing parts. Keeping the tank above a quarter full helps the pump stay cool.

issues.t: Fuel gauge sticks near half full
issues.sym: The fuel gauge stays around half no matter how much fuel is in the tank, or the low-fuel light comes on late.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued bulletins for a fuel gauge stuck near half and for a low-fuel light that may not come on until the gauge reads empty.
issues.next: Use the trip odometer to track fuel until fixed, and have the gauge and sending unit tested.

issues.t: Won't start because the immobilizer doesn't read the key
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or won't crank, while the security light shows a key problem.
issues.why: Mitsubishi bulletins cover no-starts from interference with the immobilizer key signal, for example from other keys or chips on the key ring, plus immobilizer updates for 2003.
issues.next: Take other keys and fobs off the ring and try again, or try the spare key. If it still won't start, a dealer or locksmith can check the immobilizer.

issues.t: Traction control light comes on for no reason
issues.sym: The TCL (traction control) warning light flickers or comes on intermittently.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued a 2001 bulletin for an intermittent TCL light with trouble code 12. Coolant reaching the engine computer from a heater core leak can also trigger it.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Check for a heater core leak if you also smell coolant inside.

issues.t: Popping noise from the fuel tank
issues.sym: A popping or oil-can sound from the rear of the car while driving or after parking.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued bulletins on fuel tank popping noises caused by pressure changes in the tank.
issues.next: It is usually harmless. Mention the bulletin to a dealer if the noise bothers you, and check the fuel cap seals properly.

issues.t: Clear coat peeling
issues.sym: The clear coat turns cloudy, flakes or peels, often on the roof, hood and trunk.
issues.why: Owners of 2002 Diamantes report clear coat failure at about 45,000 miles.
issues.next: This is cosmetic, but bare metal can rust. Repaint or touch up exposed areas.

issues.t: Plastic trim below the doors pops off
issues.sym: The plastic rocker trim under the doors comes loose, flaps, or falls off.
issues.why: Owners report the lower door trim clips letting go at high mileage.
issues.next: Re-secure it with new clips before it falls off on the road.

issues.t: Power windows slow or hard to control
issues.sym: Windows move slowly, stop partway, or need several presses of the switch.
issues.why: Owners report worn window switches or regulators on older Diamantes.
issues.next: Have the switch and window regulator checked. Cleaning or replacing the switch can fix it.

issues.t: Speedometer stops working
issues.sym: The speedometer needle drops to zero or stays dead while driving.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued service bulletins in 2004 and 2005 for an inoperative speedometer on this model.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the bulletin. Without a working speedometer it is easy to speed, so use a phone GPS app in the meantime.

issues.t: Loose third brake light
issues.sym: The center high-mount brake light rattles or sits loose.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued a 2006 bulletin for a loose center high-mount stop lamp.
issues.next: Have it re-secured so it stays visible to drivers behind you.
